metadata.title: Logarithmic Oscillatory Dark Energy: Empirical Fit to Pantheon+ SNe Ia and Predictive Turnaround Forecasts for the ESA Euclid Space Telescope
metadata.description: Recent cosmological data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI 2024) indicates a statistical preference for dynamical dark energy (w_0 > -1, w_a < 0) when modeled through linear CPL parametrizations. However, linear extrapolations of w(a) predict unbounded phantom divergence in the deep past. In this work, we propose a bounded, harmonic parameterization: the Logarithmic Oscillatory Dark Energy model, w(a) = -1 + A_bulk * sin((2*pi/lambda_bulk)*ln(a) + phi_0). We derive the exact analytical dark energy density evolution without numerical integration approximations and perform maximum likelihood estimation against 1,590 Type Ia Supernovae from the Pantheon+ sample. The oscillatory model fits the observational data with H_0 = 71.08 km/s/Mpc and Chi2 = 772.59 (matching CPL while outperforming standard Lambda-CDM by Delta_Chi2 = -10.86). Crucially, we deliver exact falsifiable predictions for the upcoming deep cosmological surveys of the ESA Euclid Space Telescope (z in [0.5, 3.0]): while linear CPL continues its downward phantom descent to w(3.0) = -2.04, the oscillatory model exhibits a strict sinusoidal turnaround at z ~ 1.7-2.0, curving upward back toward w(3.0) = -1.60. The resulting discrepancy of Delta_w = +0.44 at z = 3.0 provides an unambiguous observational discriminator for high-redshift weak lensing and galaxy clustering catalogs.
